setlist.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Little Red Rooster** (2 reviews): Rooster is singled out as a hot version; Bobby's vocals and slide guitar on Rooster are hot [14][15]
- **Althea** (2 reviews): Althea was a great surprise in the first set; Althea is described as way above average [15][16]
- **The Wheel** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer recalls a very long jam in the space leading into The Wheel; Release includes the space within The Wheel [5][19]
- **It's All Over Now, Baby Blue** (2 reviews): Baby Blue was especially sweet, though the reviewer admits their memory is only half reliable; Baby Blue is called great, a treat whenever played [12][16]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): Jerry opens with a high-voltage but slightly sloppy Alabama [15]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): Fans were calling it 'we will survive' during its first week [19]
- **Around And Around** (1 review): The transition coming out of Around and Around is called a ripper [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-09-23.sbd.miller.108973.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 153 min; rated 3.8/5 by 10 [1]
- **gd82-09-23.sen421.miller.12520.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 155 min; rated 3.7/5 by 10 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording quality is pretty good and consistent, though it can't fully capture being there [14]
- **gd1982-09-23.163452.senn441.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 160 min [5]
- **gd1982-09-23.153117.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: source not stated; 22 songs; 156 min [7]. Said about its sound: Patches fix Peggy-O's start and a section of Drums using another source [7]
- **gd1982-09-23.senn421.morris.100254.sbefail.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 150 min [11]. Said about its sound: Tape flips in Drums were spliced; Let It Grow has a short patch from another Senn 421 source; Left channel dropout during Around And Around was patched using the right channel [11]

## Around the show

- Listener watched from around the fifteenth row, with a friend and the friend's freaked-out straight girlfriend [12]
- Fans from Groton waiting in line by the big escalator had a friend's ticket stolen by a kid, prompting a chase [17]
- Two hitchhikers in Vermont, headed for Burlington, were instead driven to this show and back by acquaintances [18]
- Energy was high, with dancing in the halls; even concession workers danced by Johnny B. Goode [20]
- Reviewer attended with a new girlfriend, skipping the backstage 'zombieland' area where hardcore tour heads danced [23]
- Second-set song selection differs somewhat from other shows [14]
- The show starts a bit sloppy but improves; second set is strong, especially after the drum segment [16]
- Reviewer recalls a letdown at shows earlier on this tour, but now rates this show highly [19]
- The entire second set flowed together [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-09-23.sbd.miller.108973.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [1]. Also: Soundboard DATs lent by Rob Eaton [1]
- **gd82-09-23.sen421.miller.12520.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421 [3]
- **gd1982-09-23.163452.senn441.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob, Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Nakamichi 550 [5]
- **gd1982-09-23.153117.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: taped by Concert recording by Rip Tompkins, and with thanks to Richie Stankiewicz!; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 08/2021; source: FOB Beyers mics > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90 for 1st Set & Encore, and TDK MA-90 for 2nd Set. [7]. Also: Beyer recording; technical problem meant first three songs were added from an alternate recording [7]
- **gd1982-09-23.senn421.morris.100254.sbefail.flac16**: taped by Bob Morris; source: Sennheiser 421 x2 > Cassette Master (Sony TCD5M/Maxell UDXLII except Disc Two: UDXLII-S) [11]
